name: Assembly
summary: Branded client portal for agencies and professional service firms: messaging, invoices, proposals, contracts and e-signatures in one place.
best_for: agencies and professional services firms who want one branded place for clients to message, sign, pay and share files instead of four tools and an email thread
skip_if: you have a handful of clients and already use a shared drive and an invoicing tool, because the value here is the single branded portal and that only matters once clients get confused about where things live
honest_knock: Two meters run at once. Active contacts bite first: Starter stops at 50, and the step to 500 costs $70 more a month on yearly billing ($90 monthly). Internal users are the other, and they get dearer as you climb: an extra colleague is $29 a month on Professional and $59 on Advanced (yearly-billed; $39 and $79 monthly), so the more expensive plan makes each additional person more expensive too. A newer third meter is build credits for the AI app builder — 200 a month on every paid plan, $0.60 each beyond that.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 28 September 2026 in a rendered browser, both billing tabs and the full comparison table) Assembly, the client-portal platform at assembly.com, publishes five tiers. Free, a free-forever plan: $0 with 5 active contacts, 1 internal user, 50 build credits a month and 3 apps. Starter: $29 a month billed yearly or $49 monthly, 50 active contacts, 1 internal user. Professional: $99 billed yearly or $139 monthly, 500 active contacts, 3 internal users included and each extra one +$29 a month yearly or +$39 monthly. Advanced: $499 billed yearly or $599 monthly, unlimited active contacts, 5 internal users included and each extra one +$59 or +$79. Enterprise is quoted after a demo. Every paid plan includes 200 build credits a month and 5 apps; extra credits are $0.60 each up to 10,000 a month, unused credits roll over for one month, and extra apps are $5 a month each. If you bill clients through Assembly, cards cost 2.9% + $0.30 on every plan and ACH 1% (capped at $10 from Professional up); the table also lists store fees of 2.0%, 1.5%, 1% and 0.7% from Free to Advanced, invoices at +0.7% down to +0.3% and recurring subscriptions at +1.1% down to +0.5%. The FAQ says there are no setup, hosting or per-client fees, no contracts on self-serve plans, and downgrades take effect at the end of the billing period. Correction: until 28 September 2026 this field described a different company's employee-recognition plan at $3 per user; that was never the price of Assembly's client portal.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 24 October 2026 on the Free plan, without inviting anyone, without building an app and without using build credits: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We imported two made-up contacts into the CRM and exported the contacts and companies.
findings: Settings > Plans showed the Free plan with 'Build credits 50 available', '50 credits expire on November 24, 2026' and 'Used this billing period 0 of 50 monthly', while Assembly's pricing page lists '75 build credits / month' for Free. The paid plans in the app were Starter $49, Professional $139 and Advanced $599 a month, each with 200 credits.

The contact import ('Email and First name/Last name are required') mapped all four of our columns and previewed 'New contacts (2)', 'Updated contacts (0)' and 'Skipped rows (0)'. It offers 'Import only' or 'Import and invite'; with Import only, the companies were created automatically and both contacts stayed 'Inactive', not invited.

Export downloads a CSV of the open CRM tab straight away. The Contacts file had first name, last name, email, company, status, creation date and 'Invited by'; the Companies file listed each company's contacts in one cell. Both test contacts came back complete.
After sign-up Assembly opens on its app builder ('what app will you add?') with an AI prompt and 30 templates, such as a client project tracker, intake form, helpdesk, data room and contracts.
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
